thread:
Sam W: Heads up — after rolling kernel selector 0.9.2 to prod we see a 12–18% drop in tokens/sec for qwen2.5-large workloads with long context (>8k). p50 looks fine but p95 spikes and GPU util is lower. Anyone seen this pattern before?
Aya K: hmm, which kernel path landed? flash vs cutlass?
Sam W: flash_attn optimized path for qkv layout (NKV fused). Selector now prefers it for head_dim >= 128. Commit: 3b7f4e9.
Lucas T: past issues: flash sometimes regresses when kv cache behavior changes (lots of KV reuse + long KV length). Do we have profiler traces?
Sam W: attaching summary from last deploy run: 
```
model: qwen2.5-large
batch mix: 32x short(32) + 8x long(8192)
kernels tried: cutlass->flash_attn_v2->flash_attn_fused
chosen: flash_attn_fused
p50 latency: 42ms -> unchanged
p95 latency: 310ms -> was 260ms
tokens/sec: 9.1k -> was 10.5k
GPU mem (hot): +1.8GB
SM util: 54% -> was 76%
KV cache alloc pattern: many small allocs + rebinds
```
Priya R: that GPU mem bump + lower SM util suggests more memory-bound behavior or suboptimal kernel tiling on this input distribution. Any changes to batching heuristics?
Sam W: we changed batcher to prefer grouping by seq_len buckets with looser max_batch_tokens to reduce tail latency. The idea was fewer stragglers but might produce more mixed-shape micro-batches hitting flash codegen edge cases.
Ben C: Also saw a repro locally where attention head vs kv projection dim mismatch in a variant of qwen2.5 causes extra memcpy in KV layout transform. Qwen2.5 has 64 heads, head_dim 96 (kv_dim = 64*96 = 6144). If someone exported a variant with kv_proj dim not divisible by 32 we hit slow path.
Sam W: oh that's important — the model we onboarded had a tokenizer change and a tiny export script that used kv_dim=6140 (bad). But selector should detect misaligned dims and fallback earlier.
Aya K: can you paste the perf profile snippet where kernel chooser logs decisions?
Sam W: sure: 
```
[2025-11-12T15:04:03Z] selector: model=qwen2.5-large seq=8192 heads=64 head_dim=96 kv_dim=6140
[2025-11-12T15:04:03Z] candidate=cutlass perf_est=1.0
[2025-11-12T15:04:03Z] candidate=flash_attn_fused perf_est=0.88 reason=aligned=true head_div=32
[2025-11-12T15:04:03Z] chosen=flash_attn_fused
[2025-11-12T15:04:07Z] runtime: kernel fallback detected -> memcpy reorg -> extra memcpy 1.4GB/s
```
Lucas T: that kv_dim=6140 is a smoking gun. Where did that come from? Export glitch?
Priya R: QA found a couple of multi-ling tokenization edgecases that changed piecewise offsets and triggered a different weight export pipeline for some languages (CJK fallback path). It seems the export script truncated a trailing pad which changed kv projection packing.
Ben C: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) force selector to prefer cutlass for any kv_dim % 32 != 0; 2) add a cheap check in loader to pad kv_proj to next multiple of 32 at load time; 3) revert 0.9.2 on qwen2.5 pools.
Sam W: I'm leaning to (2) + (1) as a short-term. Padding has RAM cost but will avoid runtime memcpy thrash. Revert as last resort. Thoughts on RoPE scaling interplay? We also saw weird accuracy deltas when switching RoPE scaling strategies between linear and sqrt during the same rollout.
Aya K: RoPE scaling can shift numerical conditioning — when kernel changes small FP deviations get amplified for long contexts. Which strategy did we run?
Sam W: we tested linear scale (scale = 1.0 + pos/10000) vs sqrt scale (scale = sqrt(1 + pos/10000)). Linear gave slightly better perplexity in eval but worse perf due to more frequent path into fp32 kernels for stability.
Priya R: that's consistent — flash kernel assumes stable FP16 range; if we adjust RoPE to push values out of that range we go to fp32 fallback. For qwen2.X families we should clamp scale or use mixed ALiBi+RoPE variant.
Ben C: small experiment idea: ALiBi hybrid — keep RoPE for local context, ALiBi for longer positions; that kept FP16 ranges tighter in our micro-benchmarks. Could be a deployable knob.
Lucas T: tokenizer side — note multi-ling tokenizer produced longer token counts for Chinese by splitting into many small tokens which increased KV reuse and hit worst-case paths. Short-term: enable language-aware batching (group by lang then seq_len).
Sam W: action items I'm taking: 
- Pad kv_proj on load to 32-aligned (Priya to PR config)
- Selector: add fallback rule for misaligned kv_dim (Ben)
- Re-run perf matrix: head_dim multipliers {64,96,128} x seq {512,2048,8192} x kernel {cutlass,flash} (Lucas running)
- ALiBi+RoPE hybrid eval on dev set (Aya)
- QA: add tokenization smoke for CJK/western to catch export churn (qa-bot to add tests)

Ben C: I'll draft the selector change. For the padding bet — we should log a metric whenever we pad so we can alert if it's widespread.
qa-bot: Added regression test job: qwen2.5-tokenization-smoke — will run on every export PR.
infra-bot: Deploy 0.9.2 rollforward reverted on pool qwen2.5-large at 2025-11-12T17:30Z (per infra policy).
Sam W: thanks. Lucas — can you post the re-run numbers when ready? Also tag me in PRs.
Lucas T: will do, starting the perf matrix now. Expect initial numbers in ~2 hours.
Aya K: one more note — be careful with batcher change: prefer max_batch_tokens per-device instead of global so long-context jobs don't steal slots. I can sketch a patch.
Sam W: perfect. :thumbsup:
